In mathematics, the '''Perkel graph''', named after Manley Perkel, is a 6-[[regular graph]] with 57 vertices and 171 edges. It is the unique [[distance-regular graph]] with intersection array (6, 5, 2; 1, 1, 3).<ref>Coolsaet, K. and Degraer, J. "A Computer Assisted Proof of the Uniqueness of the Perkel Graph." Designs, Codes and Crypt. 34, 155–171, 2005.</ref> The Perkel graph is also [[Distance-transitive graph|distance-transitive]].
 
It is also the [[n-skeleton|skeleton]] of an [[abstract regular polytope]], the [[57-cell]].

The vertex set is {{math|Z<sub>''3''</sub> &times; Z<sub>''19''</sub>}} where {{math|(''i'',''j'')}} is joined to {{math|(''i+1'',''k'')}} when {{math|(''k''−''j'')<sup>3</sup>}} = {{math|2<sup>6''i''</sup>}}.
